lines.text: Every computer on the internet has an IP address, but can two different people share the exact same one?
The answer is yes, and millions of people do every single day.
Inside private local networks, almost every home router assigns devices addresses like 192.168.1.1.
Millions of people share those private internal IP addresses without conflict.
When heading onto the public internet, a process called Network Address Translation converts all your family's devices to one public IP.
Mobile phone carriers also use Carrier-Grade NAT, bundling thousands of different cellular users under a single public IP address.
Your IP address is more like a shared apartment lobby than a single private bedroom.
